findings.text: Architecture hooks prepare the kexec control page for use and later release it, maintaining an identity mapping while active and toggling executable and writable permissions across the transition.
Machine transfer entry quiesces local CPU state including interrupts, debug facilities and tracing, then enters the relocated trampoline and restores preserved state on return paths.
Early kexec debugging uses sixteen identical trap descriptors anchored in the control area with evenly strided handler offsets.
Transfer behavior records two independent conditions: whether processor context must survive the jump and whether this CPU observed incoherent cache state.
Segment selectors are force loaded before descriptor tables become invalid, and percpu dependent calls are avoided after that point except for the final transfer.
Purgatory loader applies RELA fixups by resolving each entry against its symbol, section base and addend, supporting absolute and PC-relative widths and rejecting unsupported cases.
Purgatory relocation fails when a symbol is undefined, common, or refers to an invalid section, and when a narrow absolute value does not survive truncation.
Post-load cleanup releases stored ELF headers, clears size bookkeeping, and delegates remaining work to the generic image cleanup path.
Physical interval protection operates at page granularity from frame numbers and counts, and silently accepts empty or inverted intervals.
Crash reservation protection covers the low reservation wholly and the main reservation in two segments that exclude the control page in use by crash entry.
Recorded cryptographic key pages are hidden or revealed by toggling their present state, with no action when no key address is recorded.
Crash protection and unprotection are paired; one direction secures ranges then keys while the reverse releases keys then ranges.
When host memory encryption is active, kexec allocations are mapped decrypted for use by the next image and restored to encrypted before freeing; otherwise both hooks succeed without action.
Hostbridge probe descriptor carries four 32-bit fields identifying bus number, slot number, vendor and device.
Default probe list holds two entries for AMD vendor with device 0x1200, one for bus 0 slot 24 and one for bus 255 slot 0, and the MMCONF base is held as a 64-bit value.
Range ordering depends only on the upper 32 bits of each start address, ignoring lower bits.
MMCONF unit is one shifted by the Family 10h base shift, mask clears low unit bits, size scales unit by 256, and the fixed base places value FC in the high 32 bits.
A system vendor match enables an AMD MMCONF probe flag through an init callback registered in a DMI table.
32-bit module loader applies REL entries for absolute and PC-relative relocation types and reports unknown types as load failures.
64-bit module loader offers apply and clear paths over RELA entries through a shared writer routine parameterized by direction.

64-bit relocation validates target contents before writing, skips no-op entries, checks truncation for narrow absolute forms, adjusts PC-relative forms by location, and supports a 64-bit PC-relative form.
Patching of live module text serializes writers with a text mutex and synchronizes across CPUs, while early unformed modules patch directly without locking.

Module finalization first collects optional hardening and unwind sections by name, then applies mitigations, fixups and unwind registration in a fixed sequence bracketed by per-module hardening setup and teardown.
ORC table preparation holds a dedicated sort mutex while publishing the paired tables for the swap callback, sorts the index, then records pointers and count in module state.
ORC preparation warns when input sizes are not multiples of entry sizes or when entry counts disagree, yet still proceeds with sorting and recording.
Module architecture cleanup releases per-module hardening state when the module is torn down.
MP checksum accumulates bytes and keeps the low eight bits; processor enumeration registers every entry with topology but counts only enabled CPUs and notes the boot processor.

Bus entries copy a short type name, enforce a maximum bus identifier, maintain a non-PCI bitmap and classify known bus kinds; only usable IOAPICs are registered under a legacy domain and interrupt entries are logged for diagnostics.
When MP parsing support is unavailable, bus and IOAPIC handlers are empty operations.
Relocation paths risk silent truncation, use of undefined or misplaced symbols, and patching of unexpected target contents; all such cases are treated as fatal load errors with diagnostics.
Kexec control transfer depends on correct page permissions, quiesced interrupts and debug state, valid segment reload ordering, and exclusion of the active control page from protection changes.
Module logging prefixes messages with the module name and provides a disabled debug helper that produces no output.
